title: Iron Man: A Different Way Out — Screenplay
retrieval_query: divided loyalty practical knowledge costly choice dramatic irony irreversible consequences
reference_policy: Retrieved literary mechanisms are optional craft guidance, never Marvel canon or a command to use epic diction. The supplied foundation alone governs this alternate continuity.
genre: Modern superhero origin thriller; an alternate-continuity Iron Man fanfiction.
reader_experience: Recognize Tony Stark and his moral awakening, enjoy sharp character-specific dialogue, and discover an earned departure from the familiar cave escape.
pov: Screenplay in present tense, restricted to observable action and audible dialogue in Tony and Yinsen’s immediate surroundings. Reveal emotion through behavior, silence and subtext; no internal narration or omniscient secrets.
tone_mood: Tense, humane and technically tactile; defensive wit yields to uncomfortable responsibility. Humor must cost or reveal something.
sensory_detail: Hot wiring insulation, grinding metal, stale cave air, damaged hearing, improvised medical care and the physical limits of a prototype.
ending_tendency: A consequential escape attempt opens a wider MCU-style universe without resolving the whole origin or predetermining who survives.
premise: Write two substantial, causally connected original screenplay scenes freely adapting the captivity and improvised-armored-escape premise of Iron Man (2008). Tony Stark and Ho Yinsen work under Raza’s coercion in a cave workshop. Tony starts alive because an external battery powers his chest electromagnet. His own company’s weapons are in the captors’ stores. Scene one develops the captives’ competing priorities and a costly technical or moral choice; scene two makes the actual resulting device, damage, trust, clues and expenditure determine a tense escape attempt. Keep Tony recognizable, but freely change tactics, supporting characters, discoveries and outcomes. Yinsen need not repeat the film’s fate. No famous quotations or recreated screenplay exchanges. This is a new alternate MCU continuity; wider Avengers connections may be foreshadowed through a plausible clue, never an unexplained cameo or a rescue that erases the captives’ agency. Deliver a film script with INT./EXT. location/time headings, short present-tense action paragraphs, uppercase character cues and original dialogue. No prose-fiction narration, voiceover, camera-shot list or Markdown code fences.

length_policy.policy: Two developed screenplay sequences, each approximately 900 words, with the existing 720–1170-word allowed range including dialogue, action and cues. Favor playable exchanges and consequential action over padding; this is a word target, not a page-count guarantee.

adaptation.relationship: alternate-continuity Iron Man origin; future cinematic-universe foundation
preserve: Tony Stark is a gifted, defensive weapons industrialist whose captivity confronts him with his products’ human cost.
Yinsen is a capable person with independent moral priorities, not a disposable device.
An improvised technological choice carries a specific cost into the next scene.
adaptation.divergence: Invent original dialogue, dilemmas, escape tactics and consequences. Yinsen’s death, Raza’s survival, exposure of the weapons supply chain and the escape outcome are not fixed. Introduce at most one causally necessary original character per scene.
adaptation.interpretation: Only authored initial facts and accepted source-backed changes bind continuity. Do not import later film knowledge into characters or judge departures from the movie as errors.

style.narrator: No prose narrator. Present-tense filmable action and audible dialogue, staying with the captives; no voiceover or private thoughts stated as fact.
style.register: Contemporary screenplay: concise visual action, distinct uppercase speaker cues, original spoken dialogue and playable subtext.
wording: Original dialogue only; no recognizable movie catchphrases or screenplay reproduction.
Engineering vocabulary may be modern but action must stay readable, emotional and fictional rather than an assembly manual.
Avoid repeated inventory lists, stock cinematic gestures and repeated summaries of Tony’s guilt.
No Homeric epithets, shepherd similes, faux-biblical register or obligatory extended comparisons.

figurative_language.guidance: Let an occasional image emerge from Tony’s immediate perception; prioritize human action and voice.

style.interiority: Express defensive attention, guilt and changing priorities through visible choices, hesitation and dialogue; do not describe thoughts the audience cannot see or hear.
style.dialogue: Tony deflects through wit and technical precision; Yinsen is specific, dry and morally independent; Raza controls information and deadlines. Offers and threats must change leverage.
style.explanation: Trust legible action; no concluding moral, inventory recital or replay of a resolved bargain.

world_rules: This is alternate MCU continuity centered on Tony Stark’s captivity; no later Avengers team or offstage movie outcome is assumed.
Tony begins with chest shrapnel held back by an electromagnet powered by one external car battery; interrupting it creates immediate danger.
No completed miniature reactor or powered armor exists at the start. Devices require visible work, materials and plausible elapsed time.
Stark-branded weapons crates, scrap metal and supervised workshop tools are available; new equipment needs a source and cost.
No suit has unlimited power, ammunition, cooling, mobility or invulnerability; damage and expenditure persist.
Building an armor shell must not instantly give it flight, remote control or a trusted AI assistant.
Only witnessed evidence and explicitly held initial knowledge are available to each character.
Pepper, Rhodey and Obadiah are outside the cave and cannot appear or communicate without an established route.
Raza controls the workshop door and surveillance; any defeated camera, lock or guard advantage needs a cause.
No character knows the identity of the weapons supply-chain organizer unless actual evidence supports that discovery.
Tony is protected from permanent death in this two-scene pilot. Yinsen and Raza may survive, be injured, betray a plan or die only through earned on-page events.
Invented twists must grow from planted clues or existing incentives, and persist as consequences rather than resetting the scene.
All dialogue is original. Familiar names and broad origin elements do not authorize reproducing film dialogue.
An original character may be introduced through current conflict, with a stable identity and knowledge limited to actual evidence.

initial_facts.text: Tony and Yinsen are captives in a guarded cave workshop; Raza controls their supervised access to tools.
One external car battery currently powers Tony’s chest electromagnet; no miniature reactor exists yet.
Tony has chest shrapnel and cannot safely disconnect the electromagnet without an effective alternative.
The cave workshop has supervised welding equipment, scrap metal, copper wiring and a restricted supply of medical dressings.
Crates bearing Stark Industries markings are visible among the captors’ weapons stores.
A security camera covers the workshop door and main bench; Raza can inspect its feed.
Raza has demanded a weapons demonstration by the following evening, but has not promised to release the captives.
There is no completed armor shell, no autonomous onboard AI and no rescue team at the cave.
Tony initially believes he can outthink captivity without becoming dependent on anyone else.
Yinsen believes Tony must confront the human cost of his work, but does not consent to being treated as an expendable helper.
Tony owes Yinsen his immediate survival, while neither has agreed on the moral price of an escape.
Pepper is outside the cave and has no confirmed location for Tony.
Rhodey has no verified cave coordinates or established communication link with the captives.
Obadiah privately knows a company intermediary concealed an unauthorized weapons transfer; the captives do not know his involvement.

world_design.setting: A guarded cave workshop and its adjacent service passages during Tony Stark’s captivity.
world_design.technology: Contemporary fictional MCU engineering; damaged life support, supervised tools and improvised prototypes with persistent limits.
world_design.institutions: Stark Industries, a coercive armed faction and a search effort without reliable coordinates.
world_design.physical_systems: A vulnerable external chest-magnet power supply, cameras, rough terrain, heat, restricted tools and guarded exits.
world_design.deadlines: A coerced demonstration is demanded by the following evening; the exact passage of time and any changed deadline must be explicit.

plot_design.central_question: Can Tony use his ingenuity without treating other people as replaceable components?
causal_dependencies: Scene two inherits only the devices, custody, injuries, trust and discoveries actually established in scene one.
A supply-chain clue is evidence with limited holders, not automatic proof of Obadiah’s guilt.
Yinsen’s fate and the escape route remain open; avoid replaying the movie’s fixed sacrifice.

subplots.question: Can Yinsen secure a joint plan without becoming its automatic sacrifice?
subplots.intersection: The escape depends on an independent choice from him, not only Tony’s technical command.
subplots.removal_cost: Without his agency the story becomes a gadget demonstration.

subplots.question: What does a visible company marking actually prove?
subplots.intersection: Keeping evidence may compete with carrying equipment or protecting someone.
subplots.removal_cost: Without it the larger universe has no earned unresolved thread.

alternatives_and_costs: Comply enough to acquire time while strengthening the captors, or expose the deception before the escape is ready.
Preserve a technical advantage or spend it to keep a person or evidence safe.

scene_designs.setting: A battery cable and a supervised workbench keep Tony dependent on his captors.
scene_designs.time: The opening afternoon, before the demanded demonstration
scene_designs.dramatic_function: Turn technical survival into a contested joint plan through dialogue and a costly choice.
scene_designs.development: Let the models choose a specific invention, compromise or revealing clue under existing limits. Establish its actual resource cost, witnesses and effect on Tony’s relationship with Yinsen.
scene_designs.restrictions: No instant complete armor or escape, no assumed movie dialogue, no omniscient revelation of the supply-chain organizer. Any original character must enter through a concrete cause.
scene_designs.choice_and_consequence: End with a material or interpersonal change that can be used or challenged in the next scene; do not specify the exact twist in advance.

scene_designs.location: The cave workshop and the connected escape route
scene_designs.setting: Only the preceding scene’s actual work and choices can support the next attempt.
scene_designs.time: Later, after an explicitly justified interval before or during the coerced demonstration
scene_designs.dramatic_function: Test the accepted plan against human opposition and an earned complication.
scene_designs.development: Stage an escape attempt with an improvised armored element if genuinely built, or another earned tactic if the first scene made that more plausible. Give Yinsen independent agency; choose survival, injury, betrayal or setback without following the film automatically.
scene_designs.restrictions: No reset of injuries, power, materials, knowledge or relationships. Do not reenact the first negotiation, force Yinsen’s death, summon an unexplained Avenger or assume later movie events.
scene_designs.choice_and_consequence: Resolve a concrete immediate choice with a lasting cost and an open thread for a larger universe, even if the escape is incomplete.

chapter_contract.arc: Two linked screenplay sequences develop a recognizable origin through earned departures from familiar events.
chapter_contract.continuity: Preserve source-backed devices, damage, energy costs, witnesses, trust, custody and uncertainty.
chapter_contract.ending: End this short episode at a consequential turn; no requirement to finish the entire film or create the Avengers immediately.

chapter_arcs: Dependence becomes a contested joint plan through a costly choice.
That actual choice shapes an escape attempt and an earned alternate-continuity consequence.
quality_contract: Screenplay presentation is required: INT./EXT. location/time headings, present-tense filmable action, uppercase speaker cues and original dialogue. Assess playable conflict and visual clarity; do not demand prose interiority or remove required headings.
Recognizable characters need distinct voices, conflicting aims and changing leverage; Yinsen retains agency.
Alternate events are allowed; fidelity to the original film’s exact plot or Yinsen’s original fate is not a review requirement.
Every scene adds a new consequential development; avoid repeated bargaining, inventories or moral summaries.
Memory is authoritative across scenes; no imported future movie knowledge, unexplained rescue or reset of resources.
Proposed twists and planned actions become history only when enacted on screen.

Any new power source, reserve, bypass or device used in scene two must first be built or acquired on screen; a plan alone is not evidence of completion. Check grammar and repeated gestures without turning action lines into novel narration.
must_avoid: Copied film dialogue or scene-by-scene screenplay reproduction.
Ancient epic diction, pastoral extended similes or imported Trojan War constraints.
Instant redemption, disposable side characters, unexplained superhero cameos and omniscient secret reveals.
Technical instruction-manual passages or mechanical inventory recital.
Declaring planned inventions completed without actual work, elapsed time or consequences.
